h1: Marriott Executive Apartments Bangkok Townhall — full-kitchen serviced apartments at 5-star standard, three minutes from Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital
intro: If you are travelling to Bangkok for treatment or a follow-up at Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital and you want a base that genuinely supports a longer stay — with a proper kitchen, in-unit laundry, and the reliability of a major hotel brand — Marriott Executive Apartments Bangkok Townhall Sukhumvit is the top-tier option in this neighbourhood. The property sits on Soi Sukhumvit 49, around 240 metres from the hospital entrance — a straight three-minute walk with no main road to cross. Opened in August 2024, everything is brand new: 264 units ranging from 43 m² studios up to 175 m² three-bedroom Penthouses, all with a fully-equipped kitchen, washer-dryer, and private balcony. Prices start from approx. THB 4,200/night, with a score of 8.9 from 404 Booking.com reviews.

body.html: Marriott Executive Apartments is the long-stay brand within Marriott International — distinct from the standard hotel offering in that every unit functions as a genuine residential apartment, complete with a kitchen, washer-dryer, separate living area, and usually a balcony. The Townhall Sukhumvit property opened in August 2024, which means everything from the fixtures to the appliances is still new. Multiple Booking.com reviews specifically highlight the condition of the rooms: "immaculate," "brand new feeling," "no musty smell, everything works perfectly" — that kind of consistency matters when you are staying for two or three weeks.

The location is the clearest selling point for anyone at Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital. The hospital is on the same soi — walk out of the hotel entrance, turn towards the main road, and you reach the hospital in about three minutes flat, no arterial road to cross. For patients who need to come back for daily dressings, post-operative check-ups, or multiple consultations, that kind of proximity is worth real money and mental energy. The surrounding street also has convenience stores, small eateries, and a few pharmacies within a five-minute walk of the lobby.
"Staff were outstanding — Riy and Tao in particular. Room was spotless, the rain shower and the large bathtub were a genuine highlight. Exactly what we needed for a longer stay near the hospital."

On the BTS question: the hotel sits about 500 metres inside the soi from Sukhumvit Road, so walking to a station independently takes a bit of planning. The hotel runs a free shuttle to Thong Lo BTS Station — check the timetable at the front desk on arrival. From Thong Lo, Phrom Phong (for the EmDistrict malls) is two stops, and Asok-Terminal 21 is three stops. If you prefer to walk directly to Phrom Phong BTS, allow 12–15 minutes; sections of the pavement are uneven and a few reviews flag this. Grab works well in the soi and is the easiest option for off-schedule journeys or arriving late.

The standard unit is a Studio of 43 m² — meaningfully larger than a typical Bangkok hotel room in this price range — with a full hob, large refrigerator, microwave, dishwasher, washer-dryer, and a full set of kitchenware. Guests who stay more than five days consistently mention that "being able to cook and do laundry in the room saves a lot of money and keeps things low-stress". One-bedroom suites (73 m²) suit those needing a proper separate bedroom, and three-bedroom Penthouses (149–175 m², sleeping up to eight) are available for families travelling with a patient. All units have a private balcony with city views.

Communal facilities include an outdoor pool that reviewers call "beautiful, very peaceful", a fully-equipped gym praised for its new kit, a sauna, and the Seva restaurant for Thai and international dining. Breakfast is included in some packages but a number of reviews describe it as "decent but nothing special for the price" — given that every unit has a kitchen and several good local restaurants and a 7-Eleven are within walking distance, many longer-stay guests simply handle their own breakfast.

A few things worth knowing before you book: this is one of the pricier serviced-apartment options in the Sukhumvit 49 neighbourhood, and the property requires a security deposit of THB 3,000 per night (refunded within 14 days). The location inside the soi means public transport is not as instant as a hotel on Sukhumvit Road itself — but for a medical stay where the hospital is a three-minute walk and the property supplies everything for domestic life, the trade-off is generally well worth it. The Marriott brand brings a layer of consistency that independent serviced apartments in the same soi cannot reliably match.

honestSummary: Marriott Executive Apartments Bangkok Townhall Sukhumvit is the best-placed 5-star option for extended stays or recovery near Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital — brand-new rooms, full kitchen and laundry in every unit, a three-minute walk to the hospital, and the reliability of Marriott service. The trade-off is a location inside the soi that makes independent BTS access less convenient, and a price point at the top of the neighbourhood.
honestChecks: If you need to step out and take the BTS independently every day — the hotel is deep inside Soi 49 and the pavement towards Sukhumvit Road is patchy in places. The hotel shuttle helps, but if instant BTS walkability is the priority, consider a hotel directly on Sukhumvit Road instead.

If you are only staying one or two nights — the rate starts around THB 4,200/night, and the value proposition of a full kitchen and washer-dryer only becomes real if you stay long enough to use them. For shorter stays, comparable 5-star hotels in the Phrom Phong area offer more central access at a similar price.

If you are expecting a 5-star hotel breakfast as a highlight — reviewers are honest that the Seva breakfast buffet is decent but unremarkable. Since every unit has a kitchen and the soi has convenience stores and small local restaurants, most longer-stay guests handle breakfast on their own terms anyway.

tips.title: Let the hospital know your room number
tips.body: Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital is just a 3-min walk away. If you have early morning appointments or late-evening pick-ups, ask the front desk to arrange the shuttle in advance rather than flagging a Grab at the last minute.

tips.title: Use the free shuttle to Thong Lo BTS
tips.body: The hotel runs a free shuttle to Thong Lo BTS Station. Check the timetable at check-in — it covers most daytime slots and saves you Grab fares for casual day trips into the city.

tips.title: Stock the kitchen at Tops Market or Villa Market
tips.body: Tops Market in the Thong Lo area (about 10 min by Grab) and Villa Market on Sukhumvit 33 are both well-stocked with imported goods and fresh produce — ideal for restocking a kitchen during a long stay.

tips.title: Book a flexible rate if your appointment dates may shift
tips.body: Medical travel dates can change. Always book a free-cancellation rate — the gap between the cheapest non-refundable and a flexible rate here is usually worth it for peace of mind. Rates climb during the high season (November to February).

faqTitle: FAQ — Marriott Executive Apartments Bangkok Townhall Sukhumvit

faq.q: How far is Marriott Executive Apartments Bangkok Townhall Sukhumvit from Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital?
faq.a: The hotel is approximately 240 metres from Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital — a straight walk of about 3 minutes. Both properties are on Soi Sukhumvit 49 and there is no main road to cross between them. It is the closest 5-star option to the hospital in this part of Sukhumvit.

faq.q: How do I get to the BTS from Marriott Executive Apartments Bangkok Townhall Sukhumvit?
faq.a: The hotel provides a free shuttle to Thong Lo BTS Station. Check the timetable at the front desk on arrival. If you prefer to walk to Phrom Phong BTS directly, allow around 12–15 minutes; sections of the footpath are uneven in places. Grab is readily available from the hotel and takes around 5–8 minutes to Sukhumvit Road.

faq.q: What are the room prices at Marriott Executive Apartments Bangkok Townhall Sukhumvit?
faq.a: Prices start from approx. THB 4,200/night for a 43 m² Studio. One-bedroom suites (73 m²) run around THB 7,500/night; three-bedroom Penthouses (149–175 m²) from around THB 18,000/night. All rates vary by season and availability — compare Agoda, Booking.com and Trip.com for the best current price.

faq.q: Is Marriott Executive Apartments Bangkok Townhall Sukhumvit suitable for long stays?
faq.a: It is specifically designed for long stays. Every unit has a fully-equipped kitchen, washer-dryer, and private balcony. Opened in August 2024, everything is brand new, and the proximity to Samitivej Sukhumvit Hospital makes it an especially practical choice for medical travel or recovery stays.

faq.q: Does Marriott Executive Apartments Bangkok Townhall Sukhumvit have a pool and gym?
faq.a: Yes to both. There is an outdoor swimming pool with the Tree House Poolside Lounge alongside it. The gym has new equipment and reviewers describe it as well-maintained. A sauna is also available. Breakfast at Seva restaurant is included in some packages.
